---
title: "GVaverage"
description: "GVaverage is the mean genetic variance of the training individuals, the trace of their relationship matrix divided by $n$ (TSDFGS returns the trace)."
---

GVaverage is the mean genetic variance of the training individuals, the trace of their relationship matrix divided by $n$ (TSDFGS returns the trace).

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | Genomic variation |
| Direction | Larger is better |
| Uses a test set | no (a test set given to `optTrain()` is ignored) |
| Score a given set | `gv_average_score()` |
| Search with it | `optTrain(method = "GVaverage")` |

## Definition

$\mathrm{tr}(G) = \lVert X\rVert_F^2/p$. Maximizing it favors individuals far from the population center.

## Use in TSDFGS

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)
gv_average_score(geno[1:50, ])
```

```{r, eval = TRUE}
fit <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:404, n.train = 50, method = "GVaverage",
                 min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain
```

The search is a random-start exchange (hill-climbing) search; see [How the scores are computed](methods.html). Use `min.iter` larger than 300 on real data and check `fit$converged`.

## Original work

Chen, S.-P., Sung, W.-H., & Liao, C.-T. (2024). Constructing training sets for genomic selection to identify superior genotypes in candidate populations. *Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 137*, 270. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00122-024-04766-y>

Fernández-González, J., Akdemir, D., & Isidro y Sánchez, J. (2023). A comparison of methods for training population optimization in genomic selection. *Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 136*, 30. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00122-023-04265-6>

**Repository or website of the original authors:** R package TSODBG of Chen et al. (2024): [github.com/spcspin/TSODBG](https://github.com/spcspin/TSODBG) (GPL >= 3).
